title: feat(json-schema): run `override` before the unrepresentable error

reviews.body: Copilot was unable to review this pull request because the user who requested the review has reached their quota limit.

> [!IMPORTANT] > The "did `override` handle it?" heuristic is a denylist of annotation keys, so any blanket `override` that writes a key outside that list silently disables every unrepresentable error. The docs' own canonical `override` example is one of them. **Reviewed changes** — full read of the single commit `708cecb7` across all 4 files, plus the surrounding `finalize`/`extractDefs`/`process` machinery and the registry and `JSONSchemaGenerator` entry points. I ran the three JSON-Schema suites (508 tests, all pass) and probed the new behavior directly with `pnpm dev`. - **Deferred throw** — `handleUnrepresentable()` records the message on the `Seen` entry instead of throwing during traversal; `finalize` throws it after `override` runs. - **Processor cleanup** — all 11 inline `if (ctx.unrepresentable === "throw") throw` sites in `json-schema-processors.ts` collapse to one helper call. - **"Handled" detection** — `structuralSnapshot()` JSON-stringifies the node minus `ANNOTATION_KEYS` before and after `override`; an unchanged snapshot rethrows. - **Docs** — drops the "set `unrepresentable: \"any\"` alongside `override`" instruction and cross-links `#unrepresentable` ↔ `#override`. - **Tests** — a 6-test `describe` block covering nesting, `$defs` extraction, annotations-don't-count, value-level cases, `unrepresentable: "any"`, and OpenAPI 3.0. I verified the happy path holds through object properties, array items, record values, union options, tuple positions, `optional` / `nullable` (including openapi-3.0) / `default` / `refine` wrappers, `reused: "ref"`, `.meta({ id })` → `$defs`, `io: "input"`, and the registry overload. That part is solid. ### ℹ️ There's no way for `override` to say "an empty schema is the right representation for this type" An untouched unrepresentable node's JSON Schema already *is* `{}`, so "I looked at this and `{}` is correct" is indistinguishable from "I did nothing" and always throws. That means there's still no per-type equivalent of `unrepresentable: "any"` — a user who wants `z.date()` → `{}` but `z.bigint()` → throw has to fall back to the global flag and lose both errors, which is the exact problem this PR is solving for the represent-it case. Worth deciding whether that's an accepted limitation or something the design should leave room for.
Technical details ````markdown # No opt-in-to-`any` path through `override` ## Affected sites - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts:503` — the throw fires whenever the structural snapshot is unchanged, and `{}` → `{}` is unchanged by construction. ## Required outcome - Either document that `override` can only *represent* an unrepresentable type (never waive it), or give the callback a way to signal "leave this as `{}`". ## Open questions for the human - Is a per-type waiver in scope for this PR at all, or is it deliberately left to `unrepresentable: "any"`? ````
### ℹ️ `JSONSchemaGenerator.process()` no longer throws on unrepresentable types The deprecated `JSONSchemaGenerator` class (exported from `v4/core/index.ts`) splits `process()` and `emit()` into separate public methods sharing one context. Since the throw moved into `finalize`, `gen.process(z.bigint())` now returns `{}` silently where it previously threw; the error only appears if `emit()` is subsequently called. Confirmed empirically. Low blast radius given the deprecation, but it's an unguarded behavior change — no test in the diff touches the class. ### ℹ️ Nitpicks - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts:398` — `structuralSnapshot`'s `JSON.stringify` is unguarded, unlike `finalize`'s own `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result))` at line 566. An `override` that writes a bigint onto an unrepresentable node (`ctx.jsonSchema.const = 10n`) now surfaces a raw `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt`; the same override on a representable node still gives Zod's `"Error converting schema to JSON."`. - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts:395` — `_prefault` is vestigial in `ANNOTATION_KEYS`; `process()` unconditionally does `delete result.schema._prefault` at line 234, so it can never reach `structuralSnapshot`. - `packages/docs/content/json-schema.mdx:237` — missing blank line before the `### cycles` heading that follows. - The PR body flags that `cycles: "throw"` now wins over the unrepresentable error. The duplicate-`id` error in `extractDefs` moved ahead of it for the same reason and isn't mentioned — `z.toJSONSchema(z.object({ a: A, b: B, c: z.bigint() }))` with `A`/`B` sharing an id now reports the duplicate id. - `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/to-json-schema.test.ts:3328` — `await expect(validateOpenAPI30Schema(jsonSchema)).resolves.toBe(true)` can't fail; the helper returns `true` unconditionally and only `console.error`s on invalidity. The inline snapshot above it is the load-bearing assertion. Matches the file's existing convention, so take it or leave it.   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6391?action=fix&review_id=4923715030) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6391?action=fix-approved&review_id=4923715030) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/31670065482/job/94352680812) ｜ Using `Claude Opus` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

> ℹ️ Incremental pass over `bfc3530` only — test-only, nothing new to flag. The findings from my [previous review](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6391#pullrequestreview-4923715030) still stand. **Reviewed changes** — `bfc35306` ("test(json-schema): cover unrepresentable types behind schema-cloning wrappers"), the only commit added since my review of `708cecb7`. - **New `applies through wrappers that clone the schema` test** — covers `.describe()`, which sets `_zod.parent` so the date node is visited twice and both `Seen` entries record a message, plus the `z.optional(z.date())` ref-flattening path. All four assertions are load-bearing: the two snapshots pin the merged result rather than absorbing it, `z.bigint().describe("x")` confirms `.describe()`'s `description` doesn't waive the error through the parent chain, and `z.date().describe("x")` with no `override` confirms the deferred throw still fires. inline.body:
`ANNOTATION_KEYS` is a denylist, so *any* key outside it counts as "gave this node a form" — including keys that carry no schema semantics at all. A blanket `override` that stamps a vendor extension on every node therefore suppresses every unrepresentable error and emits nonsense instead:

```ts
z.toJSONSchema(z.object({ id: z.bigint() }), {
  override: (ctx) => { ctx.jsonSchema.whatever = "sup"; },
});
// => { properties: { id: { whatever: "sup" } }, ... }   no throw
```

That callback is verbatim the canonical `override` example in the docs (`json-schema.mdx:319`). `x-*` extensions and OpenAPI 3.0's singular `example` behave the same way, which is a realistic pattern for anyone stamping provenance metadata across a schema. Inverting to a positive list of form-defining keywords (`type`, `enum`, `const`, `$ref`, `format`, `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`/`not`, `items`/`prefixItems`, `properties`, ...) would close it while keeping both halves of the current rule.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Denylist-based "handled" detection lets unrelated keys waive the unrepresentable error

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts:384-396` — `ANNOTATION_KEYS` enumerates annotations; everything else is implicitly treated as structural.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts:398-404` — `structuralSnapshot` copies every non-listed key.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts:503-505` — the throw is skipped whenever that snapshot differs.

## Reproductions (all currently return without throwing)
```ts
z.toJSONSchema(z.bigint(), { override: (ctx) => { ctx.jsonSchema.whatever = "sup"; } });
z.toJSONSchema(z.bigint(), { override: (ctx) => { ctx.jsonSchema["x-zod-type"] = ctx.zodSchema._zod.def.type; } });
z.toJSONSchema(z.bigint(), { target: "openapi-3.0", override: (ctx) => { ctx.jsonSchema.example = 5; } });
```
The first is the docs' own `override` example. Existing users with such an override lose the unrepresentable safety net silently on upgrade.

## Required outcome
- Only a change that actually gives the node a JSON Schema *form* should waive the error. Adding a key with no schema semantics must not.
- Both existing guarantees must survive: annotations alone don't count, and value-level cases (dynamic `.catch()`, `z.literal([undefined, "a"])`) still throw even though their node already has a `type`/`const`.

## Suggested approach
- Replace `ANNOTATION_KEYS` with a positive `FORM_KEYS` set and snapshot only those keys. The value-level cases keep throwing because their form keys are unchanged by a no-op override, and the date example keeps working because it writes `type` and `format`.
- Whichever way it lands, add a test for a blanket structural override (e.g. `x-*`) asserting the error still throws — the current `annotations alone do not count` test only exercises `description`, which happens to be listed.
````

</details>

This states only half the rule and is currently falsifiable: `description` is suppressed because it's in the hardcoded annotation list, but `ctx.jsonSchema.whatever = "sup"` — the example three sections up at line 319 — does suppress the error on every unrepresentable type. Once the detection is settled, spell out what actually counts as handling a node rather than framing it as "annotations don't count", so users can predict it.
